newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico's April revised trade surplus $50 million.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's April revised trade surplus $50 million.

text.p: Mexico's revised trade surplus for April was $50 million, down from the preliminary estimate of $109 million announced on May 26, the Finance Ministry said on Wednesday.
Mexican exports totalled 9.146 million in April, an increase of 15.6 percent over the same month last year, the ministry said.
Imports for the month were $9.096 billion, up 28.5 percent from April of 1996, the ministry said.
The April surplus pushed Mexico's accumulated trade surplus for the first four months of the year to $1.564 billion.

Accumulated exports through April 1997 were $34.190 billion, up 14.8 percent over the first four months of 1996, while accumulated imports were $32.625 billion, up 20.8 percent over the same time period, the Finance Ministry said.

April exports were up in all sectors except oil compared to April of 1996, with mining exports up 19.1 percent and agricultural exports up 4.5 percent. Petroleum exports, meanwhile, fell by 3.6 percent, the Finance Ministry said.
Exports of manufactured products reached $7.733 billion in April, up 19.1 percent from April 1996. Maquiladora exports were up 20.9 percent while non-maquila exports rose 17.5 percent.
Over the first four months of 1997, exports of manufactured products were $28.343 billion, an increase of 15.6 percent from the first four months of 1996.
Accumulated maquila exports through April grew by 20.4 percent over the same period a year ago while non-maquila exports were up 11.7 percent compared to the same time frame.
Petroleum exports equalled $946 million, down 3.6 percent from April a year ago.
Agriculture exports were $420 million in April, up 4.5 percent, while accumulated agricultural exports over the first four months were $1.813 billion, up 7.6 percent.
April mining exports reached $47 million, an increase of 23.1 percent; accumulated mining exports over the first four months totalled $156 million, up 6.1 percent.
Manufacturing made up 84.6 percent of the April exports, petroleum products 10.3 percent, agriculture 4.6 percent and mining 0.5 percent.

On the import side, Mexico took in $6.935 billion worth of intermediate goods in April, up 21.2 percent from the same month a year ago. Accumulated intermediate goods imports were $25.644 billion, up 17.3 percent versus the first four months of 1996.
The value of intermediate goods imports bought by Mexican exporters grew by 16.3 percent while those bought by other companies grew by 19.5 percent.

Capital goods imports totalled $1.342 billion in April, up 60.5 percent. Capital goods imports for the first four months amounted to $4.409 billion, an increase of 38.8 percent over the January-April period of last year.
Imports of consumer goods in April were $819 million, up 58.4 percent over April 1996. The four-month accumulated total was $2.572 billion, up 30.4 percent over 1996.
Intermediate goods made up 76.2 percent of imports, capital goods 14.8 percent, consumer goods 9.0 percent.
